subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Mild intermittent scrotal discomfort; rule out varicocele or mass.

subs.title: Findings
items: Both testes are normal in size, symmetric in appearance, and demonstrate homogeneous parenchymal echogenicity without focal mass, cyst, or microlithiasis.
Both epididymides are normal in size and echogenicity.
Color and spectral Doppler demonstrate symmetric, normal low-resistance intratesticular arterial flow bilaterally.
No hydrocele or abnormal fluid collection is present.
The pampiniform plexus veins are normal in caliber bilaterally (less than 2.0 mm) without venous reflux during the Valsalva maneuver.
Scrotal wall thickness is normal.

subs.title: Impression
items: Normal bilateral scrotal ultrasound and Doppler study. No evidence of testicular mass, epididymo-orchitis, torsion, or varicocele.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute onset right scrotal pain, swelling, and dysuria for 2 days.

subs.title: Findings
items: Right Epididymis & Testis: The right epididymis is diffusely enlarged (head measuring 1.6 cm) and heterogeneous/hypoechoic. The right testis is mildly enlarged with patchy hypoechoic parenchymal echotexture. Color and spectral Doppler demonstrate marked hyperemia throughout the right epididymis and right testicular parenchyma with a decreased intratesticular arterial Resistive Index (RI = 0.44).
Right Scrotal Sac & Wall: Moderate, mildly complex reactive right hydrocele containing fine internal septations, accompanied by diffuse right scrotal wall thickening (11 mm) and hyperemia.
Left Hemiscrotum: Normal left testis, epididymis, and vascularity.

subs.title: Impression
items: Acute right epididymo-orchitis, evidenced by epididymal and testicular enlargement, altered echotexture, and marked hyperemia with low-resistance arterial waveforms.
Moderate reactive right hydrocele and scrotal wall edema.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Male infertility workup and dull aching left scrotal heaviness.

subs.title: Findings
items: Both testes are normal in size and homogeneous in echogenicity with normal symmetric arterial perfusion.

Within the left spermatic cord and extending inferiorly posterior to the left testis, there are multiple tortuous, dilated serpiginous veins of the pampiniform plexus measuring up to 3.4 mm in diameter at rest and dilating to 4.2 mm in the upright position.
Color and spectral Doppler demonstrate prominent, sustained retrograde venous reflux lasting greater than 2 seconds during the Valsalva maneuver.
Right pampiniform plexus is normal (1.6 mm) without reflux.

subs.title: Impression
items: Moderate-to-large left varicocele with dilated pampiniform plexus veins (up to 4.2 mm) and sustained venous reflux on Valsalva maneuver.
Normal bilateral testicular parenchyma and perfusion.

bank.title: 4. Intratesticular Mass (Suspicious for Germ Cell Neoplasm)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Painless firm right testicular enlargement noticed on self-examination.

subs.title: Findings
items: Within the mid-to-upper pole of the right testis, there is a well-circumscribed, solid, lobulated hypoechoic mass measuring 2.3 x 1.9 x 2.1 cm containing punctate internal echogenic foci (microcalcifications) and cystic spaces.
Color Doppler demonstrates disorganized, increased internal hypervascularity within the lesion.
The tunica albuginea appears intact without definite extratesticular extension.
Scattered background testicular microlithiasis is also noted.
Left testis and both epididymides are unremarkable.

subs.title: Impression
items: Solid, hypervascular right intratesticular mass (2.3 cm), highly suspicious for primary testicular neoplasm (germ cell tumor).
Urgent urological referral for serum tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH), staging CT of the abdomen/pelvis, and radical inguinal orchiectomy evaluation.

bank.title: 5. Epididymal Head Cyst / Spermatocele & Simple Hydrocele

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Painless palpable nodule superior to the left testis.

subs.title: Findings
items: Left Epididymis: Arising from the left epididymal head is a well-defined, thin-walled, anechoic cystic lesion measuring 1.5 x 1.2 cm with posterior acoustic enhancement and no internal vascularity, consistent with an epididymal head cyst / spermatocele.
Left Scrotal Sac: Moderate, completely anechoic fluid collection surrounding the anterolateral aspect of the left testis consistent with a simple hydrocele.
Testes: Both testes are normal in size, homogeneous in echotexture, and demonstrate normal Doppler perfusion.

subs.title: Impression
items: Left epididymal head cyst / spermatocele (1.5 cm).
Moderate simple left hydrocele.
Normal bilateral testes.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Sudden onset severe left testicular pain and nausea waking patient from sleep 3 hours ago.

subs.title: Findings
items: The left testis is enlarged, globular, and positioned high in the scrotum with a transverse lie, showing slightly heterogeneous/hypoechoic parenchymal echogenicity.
Superior to the testis, the left spermatic cord demonstrates a classic spiral twist ("whirlpool sign") with an engorged, avascular left epididymal head.

Color and power Doppler interrogation confirms complete absence of intratesticular arterial and venous flow in the left testis, while the right testis demonstrates normal low-resistance arterial perfusion.

subs.title: Impression
items: Acute left testicular torsion with absent intratesticular perfusion and spermatic cord whirlpool sign; homogeneous parenchymal echogenicity suggests early-phase torsion with potentially salvageable parenchyma.
Surgical emergency; immediate urological consultation for emergent surgical detorsion and bilateral orchiopexy.

bank.title: 7. Torsion of the Appendix Testis (Blue Dot Sign Mimic)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Acute localized pain at the upper pole of the right testis in a 10-year-old boy.

subs.title: Findings
items: Adjacent to the upper pole of the right testis, between the testis and the epididymal head, there is a distinct, enlarged, spherical hyperechoic/heterogeneous avascular nodule measuring 7.5 mm in diameter (normal less than 5 mm), demonstrating complete absence of internal color Doppler flow.
There is mild reactive hyperemia of the adjacent right epididymal head and a small reactive right hydrocele.
Both testes demonstrate completely normal size, homogeneous echogenicity, and symmetric intratesticular arterial perfusion.

subs.title: Impression
items: Torsion of the right appendix testis, evidenced by an enlarged (7.5 mm), avascular paratesticular nodule with mild adjacent reactive epididymal hyperemia.
Normal bilateral testicular perfusion; no evidence of testicular torsion. Conservative management indicated.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Empty left hemiscrotum and intermittent right groin bulge.

subs.title: Findings
items: Left Side: The left hemiscrotum is empty. Scanning along the left inguinal canal identifies an oval, homogeneous hypoechoic structure measuring 1.8 x 1.0 cm located at the mid-inguinal canal, demonstrating classic testicular echotexture and preserved internal arterial Doppler flow, consistent with an undescended (cryptorchid) left testis.

Right Side: Traversing the right inguinal canal into the superior right hemiscrotum is a tubular, peristalsing bowel loop surrounded by echogenic mesenteric fat, which increases in size with the Valsalva maneuver. The right testis is intrascrotal and normal.

subs.title: Impression
items: Left inguinal undescended (cryptorchid) testis with preserved vascularity.
Right reducible indirect inguinoscrotal hernia containing bowel and mesenteric fat.
